newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.S. grants Cambodia GSP on more than 6,000 items.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grants Cambodia GSP on more than 6,000 items.

text.p: The United States has granted Cambodia duty-free status on more than 6,000 items under Washington's generalised system of preferences (GSP) programme, the Cambodian government said on Wednesday.
Cambodia was granted the trade benefits on Monday, Cambodia's embassy in Washington said in a message to newly appointed First Prime Minister Ung Huot.
The information ministry in Phnom Penh released a copy of the message on Wednesday.
"According to this, Cambodia is allowed by the U.S. to import (to the United States) more than 6,000 items free of duty," the message to Ung Huot said.
President Bill Clinton approved the trade privileges for Cambodia on May 30 and they came into effect after 60 days, the message said.
The U.S. embassy in Phnom Penh said it had no information about the decision.
The United States suspended its aid programme to Cambodia for 30 days after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted his senior co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6 after two days of fighting.
Washington said last week it was extending indefinitely the suspension of aid to the Cambodian government, but said direct help for the Cambodian people would continue.

Hun Sen supported Ung Huot's nomination to replace the prince as first prime minister but a U.S. government official said last week's vote in the Cambodian parliament approving his nomination as first prime minister was undemocratic because of the atmosphere of intimidation in the country.
Two U.S. envoys have been to Cambodia for talks on the political situation with various senior officials, including Hun Sen and Ung Huot, since Ranariddh was toppled.
